nodes.label: House rules
nodes.rationale: Fixed rules not up for a per-project vote: One delivery is one page; FOCUS; errors are values; no em dash; agent never commits; abstraction on second occurrence; docs are living; prose in project's language, identifiers in English. Kept because tried and needed across projects.

nodes.label: What the process deliberately lacks
nodes.rationale: No formal spec, spec delta, archiving, numbered tasks, pre-implementation gate, specialized subagents, architecture linter. Each was tried in the origin project and removed; reintroducing one requires naming a concrete error it would have caught.

nodes.label: Every layer pays its own way
nodes.rationale: A layer only earns its place if it can point at a verifiable gain that would vanish without it; 'organization' and 'best practices' are not verifiable gains. Used to reject a fifth DTO-mapper layer, folding the translation into the repository instead.
nodes.norm_label: every layer pays its own way

nodes.label: Errors are values
nodes.rationale: A failure that is part of the business flow becomes a typed return value (Result); a failure that is not part of the flow (a bug) stays an exception. Infra exceptions are translated exactly once at the repository boundary so throw is never used as control flow inward.

nodes.label: Vertical slices / folder layout
nodes.rationale: Organize by the axis of change: things that change together live together. One flat folder per feature with four role suffixes, so a change request opens one folder instead of many layered ones.

nodes.label: DRY (knowledge, not text)
nodes.rationale: DRY forbids duplicating knowledge, not text. Two similar-looking rules with different owners are accidental duplication and stay separate; the same underlying fact expressed in different shapes must be unified. Rule of three: extract on the third occurrence.

nodes.label: YAGNI and KISS
nodes.rationale: Build only what is actually needed now, not what is foreseen; speculative functionality costs build, carry, delay and repair. YAGNI has no opinion on refactors done for internal quality, only on features nobody asked for yet.

nodes.label: Composition Root / DI
nodes.rationale: Every dependency comes in through the constructor so a reader can see it and a forgotten dependency is a compile error rather than a runtime failure. Only the Orchestrator and Repository get DI; the View gets ready state, the Use Case gets data as parameters, keeping it a pure function.

nodes.label: Testing per layer
nodes.rationale: Test what a piece promises, not how it delivers, because mocks couple tests to implementation. Use cases get pure tests with no double; orchestrators get a flow test with a repository fake; views get a shape test only where a rendering conditional exists; repositories get a fake for every consumer plus one real integration test per driver.

nodes.label: Strangling legacy by feature
nodes.rationale: Migrate legacy code slice by feature, never by layer, because migrating a whole layer first is a big-bang rewrite wearing a new hat. Migration changes structure and a fix changes behavior; never in the same commit.

nodes.label: Mediator pattern as orchestrator (C#)
nodes.rationale: House adaptation (stakeholder decision, 2026-09-15): a request handler (MediatR, Mediator, Wolverine, Brighter, or hand-written IRequest/IHandler with a dispatcher) plays the role the book gives the BLoC in chapter 13 -- one event in, one handler run, one new state out. The book itself never maps a specific pattern to a FOCUS piece; this mapping is house-specific.

nodes.label: Three languages kept apart
nodes.rationale: Documentation language, identifiers (always English), and the conversation language are three distinct things kept separate so translation of concepts to code names is done once in docs/03-Domain.md and never renegotiated file by file.

nodes.label: Separating deciding from doing
nodes.rationale: /propose writes no code, migration or test, on purpose, because separating deciding from doing is what keeps scope from growing during implementation.

nodes.label: Never end silent about environments
nodes.rationale: The last thing /apply says is which environment is at which version and the command that updates the others, because the real cost is someone opening an environment believing it is current, not the missing deploy itself.

nodes.label: Domain doc is the pivot
nodes.rationale: Every concept has exactly one meaning and one code name declared once in docs/03-Domain.md, normative for every delivery, so the concept-to-identifier translation is made once instead of renegotiated file by file.

nodes.label: No em dash rule
nodes.rationale: Non-negotiable: the em dash is the most recognizable signature of generated text, and a product that shows it loses trust before it explains what it does. Applies to every user-facing string, not to code comments or documentation.

nodes.label: One-page delivery rule
nodes.rationale: A delivery must fit on one page; the page limit is not about concision, it is the test that the scope was understood. A scope needing five pages has not been decided yet.

nodes.label: What is an ADR and what is not
nodes.rationale: An ADR records only decisions expensive to reverse (database, framework, authorization model, error model); a delivery's local choice, a naming rule, or a product rule belongs elsewhere, keeping ADRs scoped to irreversible architecture calls.
nodes.norm_label: what is an adr and what is not
